title: Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage

steps.title: Tools
steps.instruction: Pull out a large pan for boiling, a frying pan, a slotted spoon, a knife and board, and something to zest a lemon with.

steps.title: Prep
steps.instruction: Before any heat: slice the garlic finely, pick the sage leaves off their stems, and zest the lemon.

steps.title: Water on
steps.instruction: Get a large pan of well salted water on to boil. It goes on first because it is the slowest thing here, and everything else takes a couple of minutes.
steps.visualCheck: A rolling boil, big bubbles across the whole surface, not just a few rising from the bottom.

steps.title: Boil the gnocchi
steps.instruction: Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water. They are ready the moment they float, which takes about 2 minutes.
steps.visualCheck: They sink at first, then rise and bob on the surface. Floating is the signal, and it happens all at once. Leave them in after that and they go gluey.
steps.recovery: If they have been swimming a while and feel soft, get them out now and be gentle in the pan. They will still crisp up in the oil.

steps.title: Lift them out
steps.instruction: Lift the gnocchi out with a slotted spoon into a bowl. Keep the gnocchi, not the water.

steps.title: Test the pan
steps.instruction: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high, then test it before anything goes in. Flick in a few drops of water.
steps.visualCheck: The drops should skitter and bead across the surface and take a second or two to go. If they vanish instantly with a sharp crack the pan is too hot, and if they just sit there and steam it is not hot enough yet.
steps.recovery: Too hot is the one that matters, because it is what burns the butter later. Take the pan off the heat for thirty seconds and test again.

steps.title: Fry the gnocchi
steps.instruction: Add the gnocchi with a pinch of salt and pepper and fry for 5 to 6 minutes, turning them so they colour on two sides.
steps.visualCheck: Deep golden and crisp on the flat sides, still soft in the middle.
steps.recovery: If they are steaming rather than colouring the pan is crowded. Cook them in two batches instead.

steps.title: Rest and wipe
steps.instruction: Tip the gnocchi back into the bowl, and wipe the pan out if anything caught on the bottom.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.instruction: Turn the heat down to medium and melt 75g of butter. This is the step the dish lives or dies on, so watch it rather than the clock, about 2 to 3 minutes.
steps.visualCheck: It melts, foams up, and then the foam subsides. Watch the milk solids on the bottom: when they turn the colour of a hazelnut and it smells nutty rather than buttery, it is done. That is the moment to move.
steps.recovery: Black flecks and a sharp, acrid smell mean it has gone past browned to burnt, and burnt butter cannot be brought back. Tip it out, wipe the pan, and start the butter again. Losing 75g of butter is much better than serving it.

steps.title: Crisp the sage
steps.instruction: Drop the sage leaves into the butter and give them about 2 minutes.
steps.visualCheck: They crackle when they go in, then go quiet and turn a darker green, and stiffen. Crisp, not browned.

steps.title: Garlic, one minute
steps.instruction: Add the sliced garlic and stir it for 1 minute and no longer.
steps.visualCheck: It should turn pale gold at the edges and smell sweet. It must not go brown.
steps.recovery: Garlic in hot butter goes bitter fast. If it is colouring quickly, pull the pan off the heat and keep stirring in the residual warmth.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.instruction: Return the gnocchi to the pan with a quarter teaspoon each of salt and pepper, and stir for 1 minute so everything is coated.
steps.visualCheck: Every piece glossy with butter, sage distributed through rather than sitting on top.

steps.title: Lemon, off the heat
steps.instruction: Take the pan off the heat, then stir through the lemon zest and the juice of half the lemon. Off the heat, so the lemon stays bright instead of cooking down.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Divide between bowls and finish with grated parmesan and a good grind of black pepper. Straight to the table while the sage is still crisp.
